previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, diaphoresis, cough, and altered mental status, and found to have presumed pneumonia, for which he was initially managed in the ICU before transfer to the floor. During his stay, he developed left hand cellulitis, likely related to IV access, which was treated with antibiotics after MRI confirmation. He was diagnosed with Clostridioides difficile infection, requiring a 14-day course of oral vancomycin. Transaminitis developed, possibly medication-related or due to underlying hepatitis B, prompting discontinuation of meropenem; liver enzymes subsequently improved. His multiple myeloma remained stable, though chemotherapy was held due to infection and cytopenias. He recovered well, with resolution of infections and improvement in symptoms, and was discharged home with follow-up plans and a full medication regimen.

#New onset atrial fibrillation
The patient presented with what he initially thought was new 
onset atrial fibrillation but some documention in ___ did 
describe a fib. The etiolgy was likely related to pain, 
potential dehydration in the setting of recent c diff infection 
with decreased PO intake and potential infection given the 
patient is pancytopenic s/p chemotherapy. Ischemia was unlikely 
given the negative trops and normal EKG. In the ED, the patient 
did not respond to two doses of IV dilt and PO dilt and was 
started on a dilt drip. The patient was continued on the dilt 
drip at 10 over night and his rate came down. VQ scan was not 
suggestive of a PE. He was then started on PO diltiazem with 
rates in the low 100s. TTE not suggestive of any structural 
abnormalities.

#SIRS criteria/Fever
Upon admission, the pt was meeting SIRS criteria with fever and 
tachycardia. Lactate was normal. There was not a clear source of 
infection given the normal chest x ray and u/a, but because of 
his pan cytopenia, fever, tachycardia, and overall clinical 
picture, the patient was started on broad antibiotics with vanc 
and cefepime. He was continued on PO vanc (started on ___ for c 
diff during last hospitalization) which was to be finished ___ 
as an outpatient. It is also possible that the fevers were a 
reaction to his recent chemotherapy. Vanc was DC'd on ___, 
Cefepime DC'd on ___. Blood and urine cultures were negative.

# Multiple myeloma. Diagnosed ___, s/p auto SCT ___ with 
subsequent relapse. He was treated with Revlimid, Velcade, and 
dexamethasone in the past but has not tolerated these agents 
well. He was recently switched to a new regimen with 
Carlfizomib, oral Cytoxan and dexamethasone (although 
dexamethasone has since been held). Started C3 D1 of Carlfizomib 
and Cytoxan on ___. Had prophylaxis regimen with acyclovir, 
allopurinol, bactrim, fluconazole

#Abdominal pain
The patient complained of very bad abdominal pain initially 
although his exam was benign. He did complain of constipation as 
well. A KUB was done, which demonstrated no ileus. The next day 
the patient had a bowel movement, and abdominal pain resolved. 
Was treated with above PO vancomycin

#SOB
The patient complained of shortness of breath upon admission. 
Wells criteria of 7.0 with high risk of PE. A V/Q scan was 
ordered to r/o PE given his history and high risk: V/Q scan was 
normal. Pt's SOB resolved.

#Chest pain
The pain was reproducible on exam and unlikely ischemic given 
normal troponins and EKG. Very possibly related to his atrial 
fibrillation with RVR. Pain had completely resolved by his 
second day of hospitalization with rate control.
